records.name: Community Mondays at William Way
records.summary: A set of Monday evening socials for LGBTQ+ adults at the William Way LGBT Community Center. Each month has a game night, an open mic for LGBTQ+ performers, and a craft night.
records.what_you_do: Play board games and trivia, perform or listen at the open mic, or make a craft with the group. You can bring your own games.

schedule.text: Game night on the first Monday, open mic on the third Monday, and craft night on the fourth Monday, each from 6 to 8 pm.

locations.label: Church of St. Luke and the Epiphany (game night and craft night)

first_step.how: Add the next session to your calendar from the Community Mondays page, or call the center to ask about the next date
first_step.basis: Open to adults in the LGBTQ+ community, with a published calendar and a phone line, but the page does not say whether you can simply walk in.

records.notes: The page shows no dates. The May 2026 date comes from a calendar link for a game night. The center's calendar page had no dated entries on 2026-10-08, so confirm the next session before publishing. The open mic venue is not stated. Cost is not listed.

records.name: Tuesday MorningsOut
records.summary: A weekly morning program for gay, bisexual and trans men age 50 and older, run by the LGBT Elder Initiative at William Way. Each week mixes talks, discussion, gentle exercise and outings.
records.what_you_do: Join the in-person talks, discussions, exercise and outings. On the last Tuesday of the month the group also meets online.

schedule.text: Every Tuesday from 10:30 am to noon in person, plus an online session on the last Tuesday of the month.

locations.label: Church of St. Luke and the Epiphany

first_step.how: Email elders@waygay.org to ask about the next session and how to arrive
first_step.basis: Open to men 50 and older in the community, with a fixed weekly time and a published email to ask, but the page does not describe a first visit.

records.notes: The Elder Initiative page is current but shows no dated events for this program, so status is unknown. The online Zoom link and phone numbers are left out. Cost not listed.

records.name: Ours Truly
records.summary: A social and creative space for trans and gender non-conforming adults, run through the William Way LGBT Community Center. Members hear about gatherings, creative projects and workshops through a regular newsletter.
records.what_you_do: Take part in gatherings, creative projects and workshops. Some are online, and the newsletter shares the links.

schedule.text: The newsletter goes out every two weeks. The page does not list meeting days or times.

first_step.how: Sign up for the every-two-weeks newsletter through the link on the William Way trans programs page
first_step.basis: Open to trans and gender non-conforming adults, and the newsletter is a clear way in, but the page does not say what a first gathering is like.

records.notes: The page is current but has no dated items for this program, so status is unknown. The page's two free yearly community events (a March fashion show and market, a July block party) are one-off events and were not written up. The weekly TransWay Zoom group and the Coffee Talk gathering appear only on older listings; see leads_only.

records.name: Philly Neurodivergent Meetup
records.summary: A monthly daytime meetup for neurodivergent adults at a Norris Square coffee shop. People sit in a circle, share what is going on in their lives, and get to know one another.
records.what_you_do: Introduce yourself, wear a name tag, and talk in the circle about your life. Nobody has to share a diagnosis.

schedule.text: The second Sunday of each month, noon to 2 pm.

first_step.how: Check the coffee shop or the group for the next second-Sunday meetup before you go, since no contact is published in the source
first_step.basis: The article describes a welcoming circle, but no contact or sign-up method is published in the source, so the way in is unclear.

records.notes: Found only in a July 2025 news article. The article says the group was founded in March 2024 and meets on the second Sunday. No group website, Meetup or social page was found, so confirm it still meets before publishing. The organizer is named in the article but is left out here. The neighborhood field is blank; the venue is in Norris Square.

records.name: Main Line Newcomers Club
records.summary: A social club for women who live on or near the Main Line. Members join walking tours, book groups, mahjong and dining outings, and a few outings are in Center City.
records.notes: Out of area: the club is built around the Main Line. A few of its listed outings are in Philadelphia (a Rittenhouse Square walking tour, and a restaurant outing with no address given), so the owner may want to revisit this verdict. The listing shows October events with no year printed, read as October 2026 because they are the next three weeks. Membership and meet-and-greet contact details are not copied.

records.name: West Philadelphia Senior Community Center
records.summary: A community center for adults 50 and older in West Philadelphia, run as part of Liberty Lutheran's family services. Members use the computer and fitness rooms, take exercise and dance classes, and join clubs such as quilting and sewing.
records.what_you_do: Take exercise, dance or pottery classes, join the quilting and sewing club, use the computers, or attend financial and retirement planning seminars.

schedule.text: Activities run during scheduled hours. The page does not list specific days or times.

cost.text: Free for people 60 and older, who also get a free hot lunch. Ages 50 to 59 pay a small fee, with no amount listed.

first_step.how: Stop by the center at 1016 N. 41st Street with ID showing your age and Philadelphia address, or call to ask about membership
first_step.basis: Open to Philadelphia residents 50 and older who can show ID, and the page invites visitors to stop by and become a member, but it does not describe a first visit.

records.notes: The dated evidence is a September 2026 newsletter linked from the center's page. The operator's directory also lists 215-290-6192 for the center. No email is published (the one shown is obscured). Found through an over-50 search, so it also belongs to the seniors lane. The page also has a Program Manager job posting, which is not recorded.

records.name: Resurrection of Our Lord Parish Young Adults
records.summary: Young adults ages 18 to 35 from a parish in Northeast Philadelphia. The groups mix faith activities such as Bible studies and retreats with social nights, including faith talks at local bars and dances.
records.what_you_do: Join a Bible study, a retreat or pilgrimage, or a social mixer or dance. Contact the parish or its Facebook group to hear about the next gathering.

schedule.text: Groups meet weekly, monthly and yearly, according to the parish page, but no days, times or dates are listed.

first_step.how: Contact the parish office by email or phone and ask which young adult group meets next
first_step.basis: The page lists several contacts, but no dates, venue or sign-up steps, so the way in is unclear.

records.notes: The young adult page is up but has no dated items (only a copyright footer, which does not count), so status is unknown. The page names the Archdiocese of Philadelphia but does not use the word Catholic, so the faith label rests on that naming; the owner may want to check it. Venue not stated; the Northeast location comes from the parish's group name. Cost not stated. Local groups on the page: Fire of Faith YA (Facebook) and the Local Young Adults of the Archdiocese, whose own domain did not resolve when checked.

records.name: PHLash Climbing
records.summary: A peer-led group for LGBTQIA+ climbers in Philadelphia and nearby areas. It holds regular Queer Climb Night meetups at climbing gyms around the city, open to climbers of all skill levels.
records.what_you_do: Climb with other LGBTQIA+ climbers and allies at a regular meetup. When you book, you choose the member or non-member option.

schedule.text: Regular meetups. The program page lists no day, time or frequency.

locations.label: Movement Climbing, Fishtown (PHLash also meets at other city gyms)

cost.text: Member and non-member options are shown, but no prices appear on the page

first_step.how: Open the program page and book as a non-member, or ask the gym which Queer Climb Night is next
first_step.basis: Open to all skill levels with a non-member booking option, though the page does not say what a first night is like.

records.notes: The gym's program page names the group and says meetups happen at other city gyms, but lists no days, times or dates (its calendar shows only a date with no class). Status unknown. The group's own website was not found; the gym page is the only source. The owner should check that non-members may attend. Street address left out; the Fishtown gym is named on the page.

No dated items for 2025 or 2026 on the listing. The listing calls itself a social support group, so the owner should decide whether it is support (shown only on request). Meetup page is a lead only. No group website found.

leads_only.note: Older listing only (from a search result): weekly Thursday Zoom social, joined through a request on a Facebook group (lead only). Not on the center's current trans page. Not checked further.

notes: Searches: all 10 used (hard cap reached). Fetches: 32. Yield is low: most search results were Meetup leads, suburban groups, or undated press items. William Way: read the center's Community Mondays, Elder Initiative, trans, community connections, calendar and home pages. Its calendar showed no dated events. Dropped with reasons: (1) Recovery meetings on the William Way page (Sober and Gay, Night Owl, CMA Philly Center City, New Beginnings NA, Sexual Compulsive Anonymous, AA): support and recovery, belonging to the support-recovery family, not social. (2) Danceteria, an older adult dance class listed on the Elder Initiative page: no schedule, cost or eligibility published, and it meets at a residence building, so ask the center first. Elder Initiative social engagement at the John C. Anderson apartments is for building residents. (3) The Phoenix Philadelphia (thephoenix.org, a national recovery community group that a Meetup page names as the Philadelphia chapter): the fetched page listed events in other cities and none in Philadelphia, so Philly activity is unverified. Recovery, so it belongs to the support-recovery family. (4) The Sober Curator (thesobercurator.com): a sober lifestyle media site with virtual events and no Philadelphia community group found. Its Dry Vibes Philly event (January 31, 2026) is past. (5) CitySocializer: a paid social platform, members 25 and older, with almost no Philadelphia events listed. Not a community group. (6) Penn DiscoverMates (pennclubs.com): the listing returned 404; the campus lane should recheck it. (7) Anthem Philly (Local Young Adults of the Archdiocese): its domain did not resolve. Not retried. Newcomer searches returned mostly suburban groups; no city newcomer group with its own working page was found. Sober searches: no city alcohol-free social group with a working page was found. Neurodivergent: one news-based record (low confidence) plus Meetup leads. Paid therapy groups for neurodivergent adults (a Flourish Psychotherapy virtual group, a Center for Growth ADHD group) are paid therapy, not community groups, and were excluded. One-off events not written up: a March fashion show and market, a July block party, and Trans Day of Remembrance (November 19), all at William Way or in the community. Leads with no link seen in results, for a later pass: South Philly Older Adult Center (membership of $7 a year, ages 55 and up, undated page), Penn's Village (aging-in-place membership), NExT (Urban League, ages 21 to 44, social plus civic), Discordelphia (Philly Discord with weekly meetups per a 2024 post), Philly Queer Craft Club (Meetup), Eshel Women's Group (LGBTQ+ Orthodox monthly gathering, 2019 listing), Sober Ladies Happy Hours (2019), The Collaborative and UnWined at Holy Trinity (Jewish and young adult gatherings, 2008 magazine article), Penn Graduate Queer Women's Happy Hour (2019), Philadelphia Spanish Language Meetup (language family), Young Professionals Council (careers family). Out of area, not written: Bucks County Lesbian Social Club, Main Line 20s and 30s Meetup, Fantastic 50s Plus (South Jersey), SoberinMontco (Montgomery County), Autism York and Berks or Bucks listings. Not used: r/phillymeetups and Skip the Small Talk (Reddit, blocked per the research notes). Free Library virtual book clubs belong to the library lane. Mistake to report: I created one placeholder task suggestion by accident during this run and withdrew it at once.
